summary: All five findings of review-lib-page-report.json repaired in tools/audio/build.py with tests. The two Quindar entries are struck (selection.json, downloads.json notTaken, local folders deleted, CREDITS.md regenerated); Whisper on the 11 remaining processed NASA files returned no words (only one-word silence artefacts). One-shots keep their attack (lead-in instead of a fade; envelope t90 within 1.5 ms of the source, was up to 9.33 ms off). The four loops now wrap (equal-power crossfade, plus a wrap-point move for two of them) and every processed loop passes the loop check. Cabin long one-shots are -32 LUFS, the landing long row -24. gainDb now states the applied gain, requestedGainDb the asked one. ratings.json SHA-256 unchanged before and after (b3e2ae5c...914cf3); no server was started, the audition check was not run. Nothing committed.

perFinding.whatIChanged: Both entries out of selection.json; nasa-quindar-1 and nasa-quindar-2 out of downloads.json entries and into notTaken with the reason (struck by the owner on 2026-11-15, excerpts contain flight-controller speech, mark had said none), the same wording pattern as the other 30 struck entries; local folders assets/audio/downloads/nasa-quindar-1 and -2 deleted; CREDITS.md regenerated with fetch.py --credits; the rendered n_quindar_*.wav/png/json disappear from assets/audio/render/downloads by the build's own cleanup. No speech-free excerpt was cut. test_fetch.py: struck count 30 -> 32, the two Quindar ids must not be in entries, selection or on disk. README text added.

numbers.verdict: 11 files, every result is a single word of the kind Whisper produces on noise; no file with words, so no further file struck. No speech mark in downloads.json said none for a file that had speech apart from the two struck entries.

perFinding.whatIChanged: process_download: no multiplying fade at the start any more. Only where the first SAMPLE is above -60 dBFS a lead-in of 1.5 ms (72 samples) is put in front: raised cosine from exactly 0 towards the first sample, per channel, then the file as it is. Fade-out unchanged (30 ms where the last millisecond is above -60 dBFS). The step is judged on the 48 kHz excerpt before the level is set. New helper prepare_download (cut, mix-down, clip count, resample) shared with the measurement. checks gained leadInMs; fadeInMs stays in the manifest as 0.0. Tests: Ends class in test_downloads_build.py (lead-in shape, recording untouched, -61/-59 dBFS edge, per channel, t90 within 1.6 ms and gain equal to that of the unprocessed recording).

numbers.method: t90 = time of the first sample whose envelope (max over channels of |x|) reaches 90 % of the maximum; source = the excerpt at 48 kHz before processing, old and new = the written 16 bit files. The maximum is taken over the file without its last 30 ms (the fade-out region), which only matters for k_door_close_1 (its maximum lies in the faded end).
numbers.shiftNewMinusSource_ms: 0.00 to +1.50 for all 29 one-shot downloads (the 1.5 ms is the lead-in itself); largest shift of the old build 9.33 ms (k_land_plate_medium_0). Every one-shot is inside the 1.6 ms limit.
numbers.otherOneShots: k_engine_low_0, k_engine_small_1, k_hit_lowboom_0, k_switch_ui_18 and others whose first sample is below -60 dBFS now start untouched (they had been faded 8 ms because their first millisecond was loud); the others in the 28 got the lead-in. Peak-mode gains of the peak-set one-shots equal the unprocessed-source gain exactly (to 0.01 dB), except k_door_close_1 (see notVerified: unchanged file).
numbers.peakMovedOfK_tick_2: peak at 0.6 ms of the source is now at 2.1 ms (lead-in 1.5 ms); level step: -0.97 dB before (a 16 dB boost of the remnant), -16.99 dB now.

perFinding.whatIChanged: For kind loop: the tail is crossfaded into the head with equal power (sin/cos), length min(300 ms, a tenth of the file); the file is shorter by that, its last sample runs into its first; no lead-in, no fade-out. Where the first and last 50 ms of the result still differ by more than 2 dB in level, the loop is started at the wrap point (10 ms grid, circular, so still seamless) where the two differ least; this was needed because the loop check also fails on a 3 dB edge level difference, which two recordings (plasma hiss, rover) had by content, not by seam. This move is beyond the brief; it is recorded as checks.loopStartMs. Tests: Loops class (length, no lead-in/fade-out, last sample into first, tiled three times: the step at both joins is not larger than the largest step within +-200 samples and not above 3x the 99th percentile, for three seeds and categories; equal power on noise; loop check passes for a file that is louder at one end).

numbers.allLoopsInManifestPass: 4 of 4 processed loops pass the loop check read back from the written files (checks.failed has no loop-seam). The level swing of plasma hiss (29.9 dB) and rover (27.4 dB) is a property of the recordings and is not part of the pass rule.

perFinding.finding: 4. Bed level given to long cabin one-shots
perFinding.whatIChanged: DOWNLOAD_TARGETS: cabin long -45 -> -32 LUFS, cabin loop keeps -45 (new lookup order: (category, 'loop') first, then (category, 'long')). Rule applied to every row: a long one-shot should sit within 8 dB of the loudness of a short one at its peak target, taken as short peak minus 16 dB (the cabin value -32 follows from it); a row more than 8 dB below is a bed level. Found: cabin (13 dB under) and landing long (-32 -> -24, 8 dB under; its loop stays -32). Other rows are within 8 dB (engines -27 vs -24, thrusters -30 vs -28, impacts -26 vs -21, switches -30 vs -30, radio -32 vs -30, weapons -26 vs -24, drive -28 vs -22, sensors and alarms are event defaults) and stay. Comment in build.py says why; test_no_long_one_shot_sits_at_a_bed_level checks the rule on the table. Which rows to move is my judgement, stated here.

numbers.landing_long_row: -32 -> -24 LUFS; no download uses it, nothing moved

perFinding.whatIChanged: level.gainDb now is the gain actually applied (20 log10 of the peak after / before), level.requestedGainDb the gain the target asked for, for every download. Test HonestLevel (limited case: requested more than 3 dB above applied, applied equal to the measured ratio; unlimited: both equal).

notVerified: Nothing was listened to; no statement here about how any sound sounds.

The audition page and its check were not run (no vite server, no capture); the engine's handling of the shorter loops and the 1.5 ms longer one-shots was not tested there. The page reads durations from the manifest.

k_door_close_1 (bytes unchanged): its source ends loud, the maximum lies inside the last 30 ms that the kept fade-out attenuates, so its applied gain (-10.65 dB) is 3.44 dB higher than the unprocessed recording would need (-14.09 dB). The brief said to keep the fade-out as it is, so this was left and is reported here.

The start-step rule is judged on the excerpt before the level is set. A source whose first sample is just under -60 dBFS and which is then boosted a lot could end above -60 dBFS; none of the 33 files does (read back), but the build does not enforce it.

The wrap-point move for plasma hiss (6.73 s) and rover (7.86 s) is an addition to the brief and puts a crossfaded junction in the middle of those recordings; whether that is audible was not judged. The equal-power crossfade of correlated, tonal material can dip or bump in level; only the loop check and a step test were run.
The choice of which table rows are bed levels (cabin, landing) rests on the rule 'within 8 dB of short peak - 16 dB', which is my reading of the brief, not a measured listening result.
audition-check.mjs, capture.ts and the page were not touched (other findings of the review); n_sls_test_fire stays in the library as a source-clipped sound.
assets/audio/cache/render-wip*/manifest.json (other agents' scratch builds) and rounds/round1.json, round2.json still mention n_quindar_*; not edited as outside my files.
